details: The US labor market softened in June, with nonfarm payrolls rising by only 57,000, significantly below the 113,000 forecast. This weaker-than-expected jobs report has led markets to scale back expectations of a near-term Federal Reserve interest rate hike, causing a sell-off in the US dollar and a rally in safe-haven assets like gold. Bitcoin, typically sensitive to interest rate expectations and dollar strength, rebounded from recent lows, with spot Bitcoin ETFs recording net inflows. Analysts suggest that while the recovery offers temporary relief, a sustained uptrend depends on clearer Fed policy signals and institutional capital flows.
title: Weak US Jobs Data Boosts Bitcoin, Eases Rate Hike Fears

details: A recent research paper from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) emphasizes that tokenization, the process of transferring financial assets onto shared digital ledgers, could significantly increase efficiency, transparency, and global financial connectivity. The IMF's analysis extends beyond cryptocurrencies and stablecoins, considering the potential digitization of various financial assets like stocks, bonds, and real estate. The report, titled "The Rise of Tokenization: Deciphering New Trends in Payments and Asset Tokenization," references the XRP Ledger and other blockchains used by financial institutions for stablecoin issuance. The IMF suggests that the future of tokenized finance hinges on policy decisions and robust regulatory frameworks to prevent fragmentation.
title: IMF Highlights Tokenization's Potential to Reshape Global Finance

details: Eurozone flash inflation for June fell to 2.8%, lower than the consensus forecast of 3.0%, with core inflation also dipping more than anticipated to 2.4%. This deceleration in price rises, largely driven by a dip in energy costs, has eased pressure on the European Central Bank (ECB) regarding further interest rate hikes. While inflation remains above the ECB's 2% target, the downward trend is seen as positive. Traders continue to anticipate a quarter-point rate hike from the ECB by the end of the year, but the recent data provides some breathing room.
title: Eurozone Inflation Falls More Than Expected, Easing ECB Pressure

details: Citigroup has lowered its 12-month price targets for Bitcoin and Ether, citing weakening investor appetite, negative exchange-traded fund (ETF) flows, and slow progress on US digital asset legislation. The brokerage revised its Bitcoin target to $82,000 from $112,000 and trimmed its Ether forecast to $2,240 from $3,175. Citi noted that Bitcoin ETF flows have turned negative recently, with approximately $3.3 billion in outflows this year. The firm expects broader investor adoption to remain on hold until a new catalyst emerges, with sentiment also affected by a rotation of capital into AI-related assets.
title: Citi Cuts Bitcoin and Ether Forecasts Amid Weakening Investor Appetite
